name: Perdigon
imitates: A slim, fast-sinking mayfly or midge nymph with a smooth resin-coated body; built for Euro-style nymphing in tailwaters and fast water.
recipe: White 50D, plus fluorescent orange for the thorax

steps.text: Slide a countersunk bead on the hook, small hole first, up to the eye.
With the hook in the vise, lock the thread on and make 6-8 wraps of lead wire behind the bead.
Push the lead wire forward against the bead to hold it in place and form the thorax foundation.
Re-attach the thread behind the lead and lay a smooth thread foundation over the wire, flattening the thread to avoid bulk.
Tie in a 4 inch length of fluorescent orange thread at the base of the lead and bind it back to the bend.
Measure 6-8 Coq de Leon fibers to the length of the whole body including the bead and tie them in at the bend as a tail.
Pull the orange thread forward between the tail fibers to split them in half, secure it and trim.
Tie in the Perdigon body material and wrap it back to the base of the tail and forward in a tapered abdomen covering two thirds of the shank.
Tie off the body material, then use the orange thread to cover all underlying material and build the thorax, about a third of the body. Whip finish.
Coat the top and bottom of the fly with thin UV resin, spreading it with a bodkin into a taper, and cure it.
Color the top of the thorax with a brown marker to make a defined wing case.
Add a drop of resin over the wing case and bead and cure it. The finished fly.
